translation: (On the upper border of the bone that rises in front of the ear, with a hollow when the mouth is opened; it is the confluence of hand-foot Shaoyang and Yangming.) He also said: When the pulse at the cum-kou runs obliquely from Shaoyang to Jueyin, this is the Yin Wei vessel. In motion it causes suffering from mania-epilepsy (dian-xian), falling stiffly with bleating like a goat; and again suffering from falling stiffly with loss of voice, numbness and itching of the muscles, and spontaneously sweating at the [regular] time, aversion to wind, and a shivering (xixi) appearance of the body. Take Yangbai, Jinmen (see before), and Pucan (BL61).
